question: Should OpenClaw accept guarded opt-in replay of locally modified packaged `dist` files during self-update, together with the exact legacy inventory-less package compatibility list?
rationale: The patch appears coherent, but it changes package update behavior and filesystem/package-integrity trust boundaries that automation should not approve without owner intent.

options.title: Approve guarded opt-in replay
options.body: Accept the default-preserve, opt-in reapply design after owner review of fs-safe replay and the legacy compatibility list.

options.title: Preserve only
options.body: Remove automatic replay and keep only recovery-bundle reporting if maintainers want zero updater-driven mutation of local package edits.

options.title: Split package hardening
options.body: Defer local override replay and land content-inventory and tarball validation as a narrower package-integrity change.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded opt-in replay
recommendation.body: Accept the default-preserve, opt-in reapply design after owner review of fs-safe replay and the legacy compatibility list.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live assignee and strongest updater history owner for the package-update/security-boundary choice.
